solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frontier having British command

parts.note: an order is a command

explanation.surface: A frontier post run under British orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the dividing line between two countries, which is exactly what a border is.

clue.text: One way to punish live leader?

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a head is a leader, as of a school

explanation.surface: Asking how best to discipline a sitting leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off the head was historically a form of execution, a punishment.

clue.text: Film disrupted Hungary's trade

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hungary's commerce thrown into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryan's Daughter is David Lean's 1970 film set in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1970 David Lean picture is a well-known film, so the definition names its category.

clue.text: Land crumbling into sea

indicators.note: something crumbling breaks apart, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A coastline eroding into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, and a country is a land.

clue.text: Pencil, perhaps, and where it might be kept?

definitions.meaning: a pencil is something that draws, i.e. one that sketches pictures
a sliding storage compartment in a desk, where a pencil would be put away

explanation.surface: A riddle about a pencil and where you keep it.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way the word means one who draws, which a pencil does; read the other way it is a desk compartment for storage.

clue.text: Weapon held up by rebel first

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gun raised by the leading insurgent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' reads letters upward, so ELFIR inside 'rebel first' is reversed; 'by' places them within those words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Referee, perhaps, who gives the game away?

definitions.meaning: a referee is one who blows a whistle on the pitch
an informer who exposes wrongdoing, giving away the secret

explanation.surface: A football official accused of betraying the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one blowing the whistle, as a referee does; idiomatically an insider who exposes misconduct.

clue.text: Place such as Bournemouth put in order again

definitions.meaning: Bournemouth is a seaside holiday town on England's south coast
to sort once more, arranging things anew

explanation.surface: Tidying up a seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday town is a seaside destination; split as re-sort it means to arrange a second time.

clue.text: Encourage to listen at news time?

parts.note: to hear is to listen
ten o'clock, the hour of the main evening television news in Britain

explanation.surface: Urging someone to tune in when the news comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's flagship evening bulletin is the News at Ten, so ten is the 'news time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to give them heart, that is to cheer and encourage them.

clue.text: Big lunch organised round front of this cabaret venue

indicators.note: the shuffled lunch letters go around the single letter
organised letters are arranged anew, so they are shuffled
the first letter of this is taken

explanation.surface: A big lunch arranged at a cabaret venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges BIG LUNCH to NIGHCLUB, and 'round' puts it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-night entertainment place with music and shows is a cabaret venue.

clue.text: Loud songs in places of entertainment

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud
airs are tunes or songs

explanation.surface: Noisy singing heard in venues of amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Funfairs with rides and stalls are places people go to be entertained, the plural matching the plural definition.

clue.text: Crime taking place in parsonage

indicators.note: what takes place in a word sits inside it, so the letters are found within parsonage

explanation.surface: A crime committed in a vicar's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence, the crime of fire-raising.

clue.text: More important kitchen item, you could say

indicators.note: signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget being ranked above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something greater is bigger or of more significance, a comparative of great.

clue.text: Willing to change a flat around, with addition of piece of furniture

indicators.note: means the word for flat is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone happy to rearrange a flat by bringing in more furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: PAD is informal for a flat or home; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flexible who can adjust to new circumstances is willing to change.

clue.text: Lacking dollars, mostly gives in

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: the suffix -less means lacking or without

explanation.surface: Someone who has run out of money mostly surrenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Lacking dollars is BUCKLESS, with the suffix after its word; 'mostly' drops the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle under pressure is to collapse or yield, giving in.

clue.text: Small room near end of apartment

parts.note: close means near

indicators.note: the last letter of apartment is taken

explanation.surface: A little room close to the far end of a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard or small private room for storage.

clue.text: One lad becoming excited, given advance

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jumbled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy gets excited on receiving an advance payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Money lent is advanced to someone, so a sum lent has been given as an advance.

clue.text: Sensible recruit takes refuge in pub

indicators.note: one taking refuge in a place goes inside it, so the soldier is put within the pub

parts.note: your local is your nearest or regular pub
a GI is an American soldier, here a recruit

explanation.surface: A soldier with good sense hides out in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reasoned and rational means being sensible, following sound reasoning.

clue.text: River captured in Vietcong offensive

indicators.note: letters captured in these words are held inside them, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A river taken during a Vietnam War offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a major African river, the second longest on that continent.

clue.text: Instrument, old, at rear of brother's room

indicators.note: places the abbreviation behind the room, at its end

parts.note: a cell is the room of a monk, a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: An old instrument found at the back of a sibling's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brother' is a monk, not a sibling: his room is a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowed string instrument played between the knees is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Locatin' protest

definitions.meaning: locating is siting, here with its final g dropped as the apostrophe shows
a demonstration in which people occupy a place and refuse to move

explanation.surface: A clipped, slangy word that turns out to be a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe tells you to drop the G from SITING, a synonym of locating, leaving the same letters as the protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting means locating, clipped by the apostrophe; and a sit-in is a demonstration where protesters occupy a place.

clue.text: Conservative PM finally secured victory after setback for Labour

indicators.note: puts the closing letter and victory behind the reversed party name
a setback sends the word backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour party

indicators.note: the last letter of secured is taken

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A Tory prime minister clinches an election win after Labour stumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a Conservative British prime minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led the Conservatives and served as British prime minister in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Fish — variety of trout — nibbling bait at first

indicators.note: the scrambled fish holds the letter in its mouth, so it goes inside
a variety of the word is a rearrangement of its letters
the first letter of bait is taken

explanation.surface: One fish, a kind of trout, taking the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges TROUT to TUROT, and 'nibbling' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized for eating, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Woman sitting on bike or horse, mostly

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: astride means with a leg on each side, as a rider sits

explanation.surface: A woman who rides, nearly always mounted on bike or horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a woman's first name, so it stands for a woman in crosswords.
